title: NeoHaskell · The workshop, in our colors
question: Stripe.dev’s structure, NeoHaskell’s cyan and violet, and Reify’s clean finish. Three focused variations of the direction you preferred.

options.label: Charcoal + cyan / violet
options.lineage: Stripe.dev’s open typography and diagrams, Reify’s neutral dark surfaces
options.thesis: A crisp developer workshop with NeoHaskell’s colors doing the guiding.
options.viewport: An open typographic introduction and cyan setup action lead into one full-width annotated application model.
options.risk: Color needs enough presence to avoid becoming another generic dark developer page.

options.label: Daylight + violet ink
options.lineage: The same workshop clarity on Reify-like light surfaces
options.thesis: An airy technical page with sharper NeoHaskell color and a clear starting point.
options.viewport: Large open typography flows into a broad model diagram, with violet structural lines and cyan highlights.
options.risk: The light treatment must retain enough scale and color to avoid the blandness of the earlier quiet guide.

options.label: Violet + electric cyan
options.lineage: NeoHaskell’s logo colors amplified through a precise developer-workshop layout
options.thesis: Give the workshop a stronger NeoHaskell presence without turning it into a toy.
options.viewport: A full-width violet model plate carries the central diagram beneath an expansive headline and a sharp cyan starting action.
options.risk: The richer color can overpower the technical explanation if contrast and spacing loosen.

canonCard.label: The familiar homepage
canonCard.thesis: The previous quiet guide remains available as the conventional option.
canonCard.viewport: A product introduction beside a simple diagram, followed by setup steps.
canonCard.risk: This is the version you found okay but bland.
